name: Beltane
history: Beltane bannocks were a well-recorded Scottish custom. An oatmeal bannock was baked for the morning, sometimes with an egg and butter glaze, and shared with family. Accounts also describe marking a piece of the bannock with charcoal from the fire. Oatmeal, bread and fresh green food are common themes in modern Beltane menus.
confidence: Documented Scottish bannock customs. Specific rituals varied by place.

sources.title: TRAC Scotland: Beltane (PDF) with bannock recipe

dishes.name: Beltane bannock
dishes.ritual_note: Traditionally eaten on the morning of Beltane. Break it into pieces and share one with each person present.
ingredients: 125 g medium oatmeal, plus extra for dusting
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan), or cook on a dry skillet over medium-low heat.
Mix the oatmeal and salt. Melt the butter into the hot water and stir it into the oatmeal to make a stiff dough.
Pat into a round about 1 cm thick on an oat-dusted board, and cut into 4 quarters.
Brush the tops with beaten egg. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, or cook in the skillet 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and firm.
dishes.safety: Eat the same day for the best texture.

dishes.name: Leek and herb butter
dishes.ritual_note: A simple spread for the bannock. Green leek and herbs suit the season.
ingredients: 1 small leek, white and light green parts only, finely sliced
steps: Melt half the butter in a small pan. Cook the leek gently for 5 minutes, until soft but not browned.
Cool for 10 minutes, then beat into the remaining softened butter.
Stir in the chives, parsley and salt. Chill until firm, then bring to room temperature to spread.
dishes.safety: Keep refrigerated and use within 3 days.
